title: Bare metal, virtual machine and container: what changes in each

videos.script: Bare metal, virtual machine and container are three ways to run the same program. The difference is one line: what the program shares with its neighbours, and what it gets for itself. {{stacks}} On bare metal, everything above the hardware is shared. A virtual machine moves the line up. Each one gets its own kernel and boots like a computer. A container moves it higher still. There is one kernel, and everything above it is private. {{kernel}} You will see that one kernel directly. An Alpine container and a Debian container report the same kernel release as the host, and three different distributions. {{cost}} Then the payoff. A container goes from nothing to finished in about a third of a second, and an idle one costs less than a megabyte. {{price}} And then the price. A container limited to a quarter of a gigabyte still reports sixteen. An image built for another processor refuses to start. These are not bugs. They all follow from sharing one kernel.
